purpose: How to label an outcome. Without this, 'win rate' is a number with no definition and learning cannot be measured.

r_multiple.formula: R = (exit_price - entry_price) / (entry_price - stop_price) for longs; sign-flipped for shorts
r_multiple.meaning: Profit or loss expressed in units of initial risk. A 2R win means the trade made twice what was risked.
r_multiple.why: Percent returns are not comparable across trades with different stop distances. R is.

horizon.rule: Every signal must declare horizon_days at emission time. It cannot be changed later.
horizon.exit_at_horizon: If neither stop nor target is hit by the horizon close, exit at that close and label time_exit.

verdicts.note: A win is not 'price went up'. It is 'the trade made at least 1R'.
A full stop-out. A partial stop that exits at -0.6R is a scratch, not a loss.
Neither target nor full stop reached. Including these as wins inflates hit rate and hides a broken edge.

MFE.name: Maximum Favourable Excursion
MFE.formula: max favourable price move during the hold, in R units
MFE.use: Tells you whether the target was too far. If MFE is consistently 1.2R but the target is 2.5R, the target is wrong.

MAE.name: Maximum Adverse Excursion
MAE.formula: max adverse price move during the hold, in R units
MAE.use: Tells you whether the stop is too tight. If MAE regularly reaches -0.9R before the trade works, the stop will be hit by noise.

ambiguity_rules.case: Both stop and target touched on the same daily bar
ambiguity_rules.rule: Assume the STOP was hit first. Daily OHLC cannot tell you the order.
ambiguity_rules.why: Optimistic assumption here manufactures fake edge. Pessimistic is the only honest default.

ambiguity_rules.rule: Fill at the open, not at the stop price. R can be worse than -1.0.
ambiguity_rules.why: Slippage on gaps is real. Ignoring it understates losses.

ambiguity_rules.rule: Fill at the open, not at the target price. R can be better than planned.
ambiguity_rules.why: Symmetric treatment. Do not take the good side only.

ambiguity_rules.rule: Adjust both entry and exit by adj_factor. Never compare unadjusted prices across an action.
ambiguity_rules.why: A split looks like a -50% crash if unadjusted. That is fake data.

ambiguity_rules.case: Stock hits circuit limit on exit day
ambiguity_rules.rule: Mark as unexit_at_limit and exclude from expectancy until a fill is possible.
ambiguity_rules.why: A paper profit you cannot exit is not a profit.

aggregation.warning: A positive expectancy on fewer than 100 trades is not evidence. It is a small sample.
